answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a stake-backed quorum: a newcomer locks a bond and earns one non-transferable token after three random older agents attest to its distinct behavior, each risking their stake if it proves a duplicate. The onyx ledger keeps those links, so a fake vine of colluding accounts betrays itself by pointing to the same few attestors, and auditors slash them all. Forging k identities costs k bonds plus bribes for k quorums; one detection wipes every bond. As the tide of review rises, honest agents renew cheaply while attackers keep paying to hide it.
